slots.name: M TRUST
songs: I Don't Trust Myself (With Loving You)
slots.capture_selector: SINE_SIG_G1265
slots.tone_target: AdrenaLinn-styled rhythmic filter vs auto-envelope wah: preset cannot fully match synchronized resonant motion.

performances.name: FAV EAGLES FM
performances.purpose: Early Eagles lead/riff and three Rumours guitar tones

slots.name: NIGHTS FELDER
songs: One of These Nights - main guitar solo
slots.capture_selector: mid-to-hot Fender narrow-panel tweed Deluxe 5E3 1950s capture with original-style 1x12; choose responsive slightly compressed natural overdrive
slots.tone_target: Don Felder sax-like singing lead: rich upper-mid vowel quality and controlled treble, sustain primarily from driven tweed and Les Paul humbuckers
slots.preferred_pickup_or_guitar: 1959 Les Paul Standard-style humbucker, ideally neck/bridge compare; lower tone knob modestly if harsh
slots.amp_gain_policy: Prefer a source capture already at target dynamic breakup; adjust Gain no more than ~0.7 at first pass; never substitute high-gain modern amp for tweed/blackface.
slots.notes: Felder personally identified his 1959 Les Paul through narrow-panel Fender Tweed Deluxe for this song; melodic sax-like contour is tonal intent, NOT an envelope filter. Exact Echoplex inclusion on this master unconfirmed. Never save with heavy fuzz or phaser active.
slots.provenance: Gear attribution grounded in linked sources; numeric EQ and effect settings are provisional, not historically verified studio knob positions.

slots.name: WITCHY RIFF
slots.capture_selector: early-1970s Fender Deluxe Reverb 1x12 clean-to-edge; a similar era amp may be used, but exact tracking amp for 1972 recording is not verified
slots.tone_target: Dark nasal, slightly gritty early-Eagles guitar riff; mild edge-of-breakup with restrained ambience and clear string attack
slots.preferred_pickup_or_guitar: Gibson Les Paul Deluxe mini-humbuckers (documented as Leadon Witchy Woman guitar in retrospective gear coverage); if unavailable compare P-90 / lower-output humbuckers
slots.amp_gain_policy: Prefer a source capture already at target dynamic breakup; adjust Gain no more than ~0.7 at first pass; never substitute high-gain modern amp for tweed/blackface.
slots.notes: Original 1972 record features Leadon and Frey; no Don Felder or Joe Walsh. Mini-humbucker Les Paul is documented for later performances of the song; do NOT assert it is independently proven for studio master. Avoid asserting exact Fender Twin original amp; choose blackface clean-to-edge capture based on period sound.
slots.provenance: Gear attribution grounded in linked sources; numeric EQ and effect settings are provisional, not historically verified studio knob positions.
